sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity in Russia (June 2025, page updated 12 Aug 2026). Federal picture: same-sex activity not criminalised but marriage and gender transition banned, no constitutional or statutory protections, trans healthcare effectively banned in 2023; the 'gay propaganda' law carries fines up to 400,000 rubles (individuals) or 4,000,000 (organisations) or detention up to 15 days, with repeat offences criminal (up to 4 years); the 2023 'extremist' designation exposes participants to 2-6 years and organisers to 6-10 years. Notes 139 people affected by anti-LGBT laws Dec 2022-Mar 2024, and identifies the North Caucasus, trans people and public advocates as facing persecution — no sub-national variation within the rest of the country.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (Cloudflare block served instead of content); the underlying US State Department travel advisory for Russia advises against all travel, warns that foreigners found guilty of violating the 'propaganda' law may be detained up to 15 days and deported, and that displaying rainbow symbols is a crime — country-wide federal rules with no sub-national variation flagged.

sources.title: Russia: Rising Toll of LGBT ‘Extremism’ Designation | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch report, 30 June 2025: 101 'extremism'-related convictions (about 98 administrative, 3 criminal) for allegedly participating in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its alleged symbols; the designation took effect January 2024. Enforcement machinery is federal (court websites and official channels), with no region-specific concentration outside the areas already known.
